Industries

Regulated sectors, specific operational realities

Each sector has its own operational pressures and supervisory expectations. We adjust the workflow, the AI opportunities and the governance requirements to fit, rather than applying one template.

Industry 01

Financial Services

Banks, building societies, wealth managers and asset managers facing growing operational and regulatory load.

Challenges

  • Legacy processes spanning multiple business lines
  • Regulatory change arriving faster than operations can absorb it
  • Quality and evidence gaps exposed in supervisory reviews

Workflows

  • Financial crime alert and case management
  • Client onboarding and periodic review
  • Complaints handling and root cause analysis

AI opportunities

  • Case summarisation for investigators
  • Document extraction for onboarding packs
  • Complaint theme detection with human review

Governance requirements

  • Model and AI use-case registers aligned to model risk policy
  • Consumer duty and fair treatment considerations in customer-facing automation
  • Evidence standards agreed with internal audit

Industry 02

FinTech

Scaling lenders, neobanks and digital platforms that must grow operations as fast as their customer base.

Challenges

  • Operations built for launch rather than for licence conditions
  • Manual processes that scale poorly with customer growth
  • Regulators asking for controls that were never formally designed

Workflows

  • Onboarding and identity verification
  • Transaction monitoring alert handling
  • Customer support escalations with compliance impact

AI opportunities

  • Automated document checks with exception queues
  • Support triage and suggested responses for agents
  • Monitoring alert enrichment

Governance requirements

  • Controls designed before scale-up, not after
  • Clear ownership between product, operations and compliance
  • Regulator-ready evidence from day one of each licence activity

Industry 03

Payments

Payment institutions and merchant acquirers handling high volumes, tight timelines and intense financial crime scrutiny.

Challenges

  • Volume spikes that overwhelm manual review
  • Merchant risk decisions made inconsistently across teams
  • Sanctions and fraud signals arriving in separate queues

Workflows

  • Merchant onboarding and enhanced due diligence
  • Dispute and chargeback case management
  • Sanctions alert disposition

AI opportunities

  • Merchant document extraction and verification
  • Dispute narrative drafting
  • Alert clustering to reduce duplicate review

Governance requirements

  • Thresholds and routing rules under version control
  • Decision rationale required for every merchant exit
  • Sampling and QA designed into high-volume queues

Industry 04

Insurance

Insurers and intermediaries with complex claims, distribution oversight and growing fraud and conduct obligations.

Challenges

  • Claims processes with long manual tails
  • Intermediary oversight evidenced through periodic spreadsheets
  • Fraud referral handling split across claims and compliance

Workflows

  • Claims triage and referral
  • Intermediary monitoring and remediation
  • Fraud investigation case management

AI opportunities

  • Claims document summarisation
  • Referral prioritisation with reviewer override
  • Intermediary complaint pattern detection

Governance requirements

  • Fair outcome evidence for customer-facing decisions
  • Audit trails for referral and decline decisions
  • Clear limits on automated claims decisions

Industry 05

RegTech

Technology providers whose products must themselves operate to the controls they help clients meet.

Challenges

  • Product roadmaps moving faster than internal operational controls
  • Client implementations that depend on custom services work
  • Customer-facing commitments without matching internal evidence

Workflows

  • Client implementation and change control
  • Support escalation with data access governance
  • Internal control testing for product claims

AI opportunities

  • Implementation documentation drafting
  • Support triage with access-aware routing
  • Release note and change impact analysis

Governance requirements

  • Internal controls evidenced for each client-facing assurance claim
  • Data access logged and reviewed
  • Vendor and sub-processor governance aligned to client requirements

Industry 06

Professional Services

Law, accounting and advisory firms with client acceptance, conflicts and anti-money laundering obligations.

Challenges

  • Client acceptance processes split across partners and support teams
  • Conflict checks run inconsistently
  • AML supervision evidence assembled at renewal time

Workflows

  • Client and matter acceptance
  • Conflict clearance
  • Periodic AML review and training records

AI opportunities

  • Entity research summaries for acceptance reviews
  • Conflict search result triage
  • Policy question answering for staff, with citations

Governance requirements

  • Partner sign-off recorded for high-risk acceptances
  • Supervisory evidence maintained continuously
  • Client confidentiality controls on AI tools
